title: Minimum Removals to Achieve Target XOR
summary: Given an integer array nums and a target integer, determine the least number of elements to remove from nums so that the bitwise XOR of the remaining elements matches the target.
statement: Given an integer array nums and a target integer, determine the least number of elements to remove from nums so that the bitwise XOR of the remaining elements matches the target. If achieving the target is impossible, return -1. The bitwise XOR of an empty array is defined as 0.
constraints: nums is nonempty and contains nonnegative integers.
Remove any elements so the XOR of those remaining equals target; empty XOR is zero.
Return the fewest removals, or -1 if target cannot be formed.
hints: Minimizing removals is equivalent to maximizing how many kept elements produce the target XOR.
Maintain a map from reachable XOR to the greatest kept count after each element.
For every state, either skip the element or keep it and transition to xor^value.
The two transitions enumerate every subset, while retaining only the greatest count is safe for all future XOR operations.
editorial: The two transitions enumerate every subset, while retaining only the greatest count is safe for all future XOR operations.

tests.explanation: Keeping one and three gives XOR two, so removing only the value two is optimal.
Remove the sole element to obtain empty XOR zero, costing one removal.
